queries.question: Should the cache layer load missing data on behalf of the application?
Should writes land in the cache first and reach the store asynchronously?
Should entries expire after a bounded time even without an explicit invalidation?
Should concurrent misses be coordinated so they do not all hit the source at once?
Should data be cached in more than one tier with different latency and freshness?
Should data be split across shards by a partition key to scale beyond one node?
Should keys and nodes share a hash ring so membership changes move only a fraction of data?
Should read-only replicas serve queries to offload the writer?
Should a separate lookup table maintain a secondary access path?
Should data be backfilled while the system continues serving reads and writes?
Should different data responsibilities use different stores while one authoritative boundary owns consistency?
Should a failed call be retried after increasing delays?
Should each call have a bounded wait before it is treated as failed?
Should a failed primary path return a defined degraded result?
Should request rate be limited to protect a dependency or budget?
Should work be buffered in a queue so producers and consumers can run at different rates?
Should an external monitor distinguish liveness, readiness and startup health?
Should one node be chosen to coordinate work while others stand by?
Should a shared lock prevent concurrent access to one resource across processes?
Should decisions require a majority of replicas rather than one node?
